rules.statement: A transfer starts with a one-cycle Setup phase (PSEL high, PENABLE low), followed by the Access phase (PENABLE high), which ends in the cycle where PREADY is high.

rules.condition: after the cycle where PREADY is high
rules.statement: After PREADY the bus may return to IDLE or go directly to the Setup phase of the next transfer.
PADDR, PPROT, PENABLE, PWRITE, PAUSER, PSTRB, active PWDATA lanes and PWUSER of a write are valid whenever PSEL is high; the bridge captures them in the Setup cycle.
PREADY is valid when PSEL and PENABLE are high.

rules.condition: PSEL, PENABLE and PREADY are high
rules.statement: PRDATA of a read, PSLVERR, PRUSER of a read and PBUSER are valid when PSEL, PENABLE and PREADY are high.

rules.condition: between the Setup and Access phase and while PREADY is low
rules.statement: PADDR, PPROT, PWRITE, PWDATA, PSTRB, PAUSER and PWUSER must not change between Setup and Access phase and while PREADY is low.
The bridge guarantees stability of the completer-side fields by loading them into reg_apb_payload once, relying on requester stability only in the Setup cycle.

rules.condition: completer extends the Access phase with PREADY low
rules.statement: The bridge raises the requester-side PREADY only after the completer-side PREADY.
PSLVERR is valid only in the last cycle of a transfer.

rules.condition: a transfer completes with an error
rules.statement: The bridge forwards PRDATA and PSLVERR together without masking, even for a read with an error.
PSTRB must be low in a read.
The bridge forwards PSTRB as received.

rules.condition: APB5; PWAKEUP high in the same cycle as PSEL
rules.statement: PWAKEUP must be glitch-free to be sampled asynchronously and must stay high until PREADY when high in the same cycle as PSEL.
PWAKEUP may be asserted before, during or after PSEL.
PWAKEUP should be asserted one cycle before PSEL.
A completer may wait for PWAKEUP before driving PREADY.
PAUSER and PWUSER are valid with PSEL (PWUSER also with PWRITE) and keep their value through Setup and Access phases.
PRUSER and PBUSER are valid in the PREADY cycle.
A domain-crossing bridge should provide all user signals.

rules.condition: write or read without wait states, completer PREADY in the first Access cycle
rules.statement: The bridge performs one completer-side transfer and returns the response.

rules.condition: completer holds PREADY low for any number of cycles
rules.statement: Requester-side PREADY stays low until the completer response.
The bridge returns PSLVERR with PREADY and forwards the data.

rules.condition: next Setup phase immediately after PREADY
rules.statement: The bridge accepts a back-to-back transfer whose Setup phase follows right after PREADY.

rules.condition: PENABLE high without a preceding Setup cycle
rules.statement: The bridge ignores PENABLE high without a preceding Setup cycle and starts no transfer.

rules.condition: requester changes a field during the Access phase
rules.statement: The bridge does not detect the change and uses the values captured in the Setup phase.
The bridge waits without limit for the completer PREADY.
A single reset asserted alone is not supported; both resets must be asserted together, and a transfer in flight is lost on reset.

rules.condition: reset in the middle of a transfer
rules.statement: The transfer in flight is lost when reset is asserted mid-transfer.
The IP has no interrupt or event output; errors travel as PSLVERR of the transfer.
